title: Brussels Bomber Command Memorial

external_narratives.summary: The Bomber Command Memorial in London incorporates aluminium recovered from a Halifax III bomber shot down over Belgium on 12 May 1944. While this is the London memorial, it has a direct connection to Belgium where eight crew were killed. Three crew members were found still at their stations when the aircraft was excavated in 1997 and buried in Belgium with full military honours.
key_details: Halifax III shot down over Belgium, 12 May 1944
Three crew found at stations and buried in Belgium with military honours

memorial_details:
About the Memorial | Bomber Command Memorial Located in London's Green Park, the Bomber Command Memorial has been built to be modern, yet classical, in Portland stone.

The memorial was officially unveiled by Her Majesty The Queen on 28 June 2012.

The Bomber Command Memorial, located in London's Green Park, was built with Portland stone and features bronze sculptures of a Bomber Command aircrew at its heart.

The memorial was officially unveiled by Her Majesty The Queen on 28 June 2012.

Official Unveiling (2012-06-28): Her Majesty The Queen officially unveiled the Bomber Command Memorial.
